entities.name: Asmara Cinema-Teatro
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Asmara Cinema Teatro (also known as the Cinema Teatro Asmara or the Odeon Cinema) in Asmara, Eritrea, is part of Asmara's extraordinary collection of Italian Modernist architecture — the most intact collection of Rationalist, Art Deco, and Futurist buildings from the Italian colonial period in the world, which led to Asmara's designation as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2017, the first 20th-century city to receive this designation. Asmara was built as the 'piccola Roma' (little Rome) of Italian East Africa under Mussolini's colonial administration.

Asmara's Italian colonial architecture (primarily built 1935-1941) represents a unique historical moment: Mussolini's Ethiopian campaign (1935-1936) made Eritrea the base for Italian East Africa, and Italian architects were given an extraordinary commission to build a model fascist colonial city at altitude in the tropics — applying the latest European Modernist architectural styles (Rationalism, Art Deco, Futurism) to a city being constructed nearly from scratch. The result is an architectural museum of 1930s Modernism: the FIAT Tagliero service station (a reinforced concrete masterpiece), the Cinema Impero, the Opera House, and dozens of other buildings in an remarkably complete state of preservation.

The Cinema Teatro is part of this ensemble — a cinema-theater typical of Italian colonial cultural life, providing entertainment and cultural programming for the Italian colonial population while also reflecting the Modernist aesthetic values that Italian architecture was promoting worldwide in the 1930s. Asmara's preservation resulted partly from post-independence Eritrean appreciation of this architectural heritage as a unique national asset.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Asmara Cinema Teatro — part of the world's most intact collection of 1930s Italian Rationalist architecture in Asmara's UNESCO World Heritage site, the first 20th-century city so designated — is historically significant as a monument of Italian fascist colonial architecture preserved as African heritage.
